content.title: What is Polymorphism?
content.description: Polymorphism is an Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concept that allows the same method or interface to perform different actions depending on the object or parameters involved. The word 'Polymorphism' means 'many forms'.

content.content: Polymorphism enables one interface to represent multiple implementations. In Java, polymorphism allows the same method name to behave differently based on the object or method parameters. It improves flexibility, extensibility, and code reusability.

content.title: Why Use Polymorphism?
content.content: Polymorphism allows developers to write generic, reusable code while enabling different objects to provide their own implementations.
Java supports two main types of polymorphism: Compile-Time Polymorphism (Method Overloading) and Runtime Polymorphism (Method Overriding).

content.title: Two Forms of Polymorphism
content.description: Compile-time polymorphism depends on method signatures, while runtime polymorphism depends on the actual object created.

content.content: Method overloading occurs when multiple methods have the same name but different parameter lists. The compiler decides which method to call based on the arguments.

content.title: Method Overloading Example

content.content: Method overriding occurs when a child class provides its own implementation of a method already defined in the parent class. The JVM determines which method to execute at runtime.

content.title: Method Overriding Example
Dynamic Method Dispatch
content.content: Runtime polymorphism is implemented using dynamic method dispatch, where the JVM decides which overridden method to execute based on the actual object.

items.question: Can overloaded methods have different parameter types?
items.answer: Yes. Parameter types, numbers, or order must differ.

items.question: Can methods be overloaded only by changing the return type?
items.answer: No. Changing only the return type does not create a valid overloaded method.

items.question: Can constructors be overloaded?
items.answer: Yes. Constructor overloading is commonly used.

content.content: To override a method, the child class method must have the same name, parameters, and compatible return type as the parent class method.

content.title: Overriding Example

items.question: Code Reusability
items.answer: Write generic code that works with different object types.

items.question: Flexibility
items.answer: Programs become easier to extend without changing existing code.

items.question: Scalability
items.answer: New classes can be added with minimal changes.

content.title: Remote Control
content.content: A TV remote has the same Power button, but pressing it performs different actions depending on whether it's connected to a TV, projector, or smart device. Similarly, the same method call behaves differently depending on the object.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Polymorphism is one of the four pillars of OOP. Interviewers frequently ask about method overloading, method overriding, dynamic method dispatch, and the differences between compile-time and runtime polymorphism.

items.question: Can methods be overloaded by changing only the return type?
items.answer: No. The parameter list must also be different.

items.question: Can static methods be overridden?
items.answer: No. Static methods are hidden, not overridden.

items.question: Does runtime polymorphism work without inheritance?
items.answer: No. It requires inheritance and method overriding.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Method overloading provides compile-time polymorphism, while method overriding provides runtime polymorphism. Together, they make Java programs more flexible and reusable.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Java supports compile-time and runtime polymorphism.
Dynamic method dispatch allows the JVM to call the correct overridden method.
